title: "FCS Enrichment - `r params$project_name`"
subtitle: "`r if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$traitname)) paste0('Trait: ', params$traitname) else if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$trait)) paste0('Trait: ', params$trait) else if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$project_name)) paste0('Project: ', params$project_name) else ''`"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d %B %Y')`"
author: "PhyloPhere pipeline"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: flatly
    syntax_highlighting: tango
    toc: true
    toc_float:
      collapsed: false
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
    fig_width: 10
    fig_height: 6
    self_contained: true
    mathjax: null                       # no math in this report
    md_extensions: "-tex_math_dollars"  # gene-set names contain '$' (e.g. V$HNF4_01) - never parse as TeX math
params:
  stats_file:   NULL          # TSV: gene + one-or-more score_<ranking> cols + optional flag_<name> cols
  universe_file: NULL         # cleaned_background (one gene symbol per line)
  gmt_dir:      NULL          # directory of curated *.gmt files
  project_name: "FCS"
  num_g:        10            # min genes per set (fastwilcoxGMT num.g)
  max_g:        0             # max genes per set (0 / Inf = no limit)
  fdr_thr:      0.15          # BH threshold on the permulation p of each set (q.perm), per ranking and database
  pperm_thr:    0.025         # raw permulation-p threshold of the Redlich rule
  gene_stat: "max"      # gene statistic of the observed gene scores; the CAAS null must hold the same one
  score_source: "caas"       # pipeline source: caas (zero floor) or rer (exclude missing statistics)
  analytic_levels: "0.05,0.1,0.15" # analytic rule (Redlich et al. 2024): BH levels of the analytic p, with p.perm < pperm_thr
  cluster_similarity: "jaccard" # redundancy reduction: leading-edge similarity, jaccard or overlap
  cluster_threshold:  0.5     # redundancy reduction: similarity at which a set joins a representative
  top_n:        20            # rows shown per database x ranking
  leading_edge_top_n: 100     # rows shown in the pooled (all-database) leading-edge
                              # composition table, deliberately more generous than
                              # top_n, which caps a single database's slice, not the
                              # whole significant set for a ranking. A term that IS
                              # significant but ranks outside this cap will silently
                              # disappear from the on-page table (though never from
                              # fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge.tsv, which is unbounded).
  traitname:    "trait"
  perms_file:   "NO_FILE"
  enrich_file:  NULL          # pre-computed, GMT-batch-merged fcs_run_all() output (see fcs_compute.R /
                              # FCS_COMPUTE_BATCHED+FCS_CONCAT in fcs.nf). When NULL, falls back to running
                              # fcs_run_all() here directly (unbatched path, e.g. ad-hoc/manual rendering)
  annot_file:   "NO_FILE"     # optional cross-module annotation overlay (SCORING fcs_stats.tsv):
                              # supplies flag_* + CAAS nominal/BH evidence for the leading edge.
                              # When NO_FILE, annotation falls back to the stats file itself.
---

<!-- PhyloPhere | subworkflows/ENRICHMENT/local/ -->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7, dev = "png", dpi = 200)

# ── Dependencies ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(knitr)
  library(kableExtra)
  library(patchwork)
})

# Reuse the settings saved with the exact calibrated input on independent renders.
# The GUI supplies defaults; these must not relabel an existing run's statistic,
# significance rules, set-size filters or redundancy groups.
if (!is.null(params$enrich_file) && file.exists(params$enrich_file)) {
  saved_metadata <- file.path(dirname(params$enrich_file), "fcs_report_metadata.json")
  if (file.exists(saved_metadata)) {
    # rmarkdown locks the params binding; temporarily unlock it to restore
    # the settings saved with these data, then retain the original lock state.
    .params_env <- knitr::knit_global()
    .params_locked <- bindingIsLocked("params", .params_env)
    if (.params_locked) unlockBinding("params", .params_env)
    saved_params <- jsonlite::read_json(saved_metadata, simplifyVector = TRUE)
    keys <- intersect(names(saved_params), c("gene_stat", "score_source", "num_g", "max_g",
      "fdr_thr", "pperm_thr", "analytic_levels", "cluster_similarity", "cluster_threshold"))
    for (key in keys) params[[key]] <- saved_params[[key]]
    if (.params_locked) lockBinding("params", .params_env)
  }
}

# ── Theme and helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(l = 20, r = 20)),
    axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)),
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", hjust = 0, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 10)),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)
  )
)
# Pin the dplyr verbs so that loaded packages cannot mask them.
filter <- dplyr::filter; select <- dplyr::select; rename <- dplyr::rename
mutate <- dplyr::mutate; arrange <- dplyr::arrange
# Fallback operator: b when a is NULL, empty or an empty string.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (!is.null(a) && length(a) > 0 && nzchar(as.character(a)[1])) a else b

# Load the shared FCS core (fcs_enrich.R). The process copies local/* into the work
# directory, so src/ sits next to this file; the other candidates cover manual renders.
this_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input(), mustWork = FALSE)),
                     error = function(e) ".")
src_candidates <- c(file.path(this_dir, "src", "fcs_enrich.R"), "src/fcs_enrich.R", file.path(this_dir, "fcs_enrich.R"), "fcs_enrich.R")
src <- src_candidates[file.exists(src_candidates)][1]
if (is.na(src)) stop("fcs_enrich.R not found under src/ or next to FCS_general.Rmd")
suppressMessages(invisible(capture.output(source(src))))
src_cluster <- file.path(dirname(src), "fcs_cluster.R")
if (!file.exists(src_cluster)) stop("fcs_cluster.R not found next to fcs_enrich.R")
source(src_cluster)

# HTML table with the report style; optional scroll box of fixed height.
kbl_html <- function(df, height = NULL, escape = TRUE, caption = NULL, ...) {
  k <- kable(df, format = "html", escape = escape, caption = caption, ...) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(height)) k <- scroll_box(k, height = height)
  k
}
```

```{r load, include=FALSE}
# ── Inputs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
stopifnot(!is.null(params$stats_file), file.exists(params$stats_file))
stopifnot(!is.null(params$universe_file), file.exists(params$universe_file))

stats <- readr::read_tsv(params$stats_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
if (!"gene" %in% names(stats)) {
  gcol <- intersect(c("Gene", "GENE"), names(stats))[1]
  if (!is.na(gcol)) stats <- dplyr::rename(stats, gene = !!gcol)
}
stopifnot("gene" %in% names(stats))

# Universe: the cleaned background (all tested genes). It falls back to the scored genes
# when no valid background is given (for instance a NO_* sentinel file).
universe <- character(0)
if (!is.null(params$universe_file) && file.exists(params$universe_file) &&
    !grepl("^NO_", basename(params$universe_file))) {
  universe <- unique(trimws(readLines(params$universe_file)))
  universe <- universe[nzchar(universe)]
}
if (length(universe) < 2) {
  message("No valid universe file - falling back to scored genes as the universe.")
  universe <- unique(stats$gene)
}

score_cols <- grep("^score_", names(stats), value = TRUE)
if (length(score_cols) == 0) stop("stats_file has no score_<ranking> columns")
ranking_names_raw <- sub("^score_", "", score_cols)
# Canonical tab order: global, top, bottom. The column order of stats_file is incidental and
# must not drive it; a ranking outside this set is appended at the end in file order.
RANKING_ORDER <- c("global", "top", "bottom")
ranking_names <- c(intersect(RANKING_ORDER, ranking_names_raw),
                   setdiff(ranking_names_raw, RANKING_ORDER))

# Annotation overlay: the cross-module leading-edge flags (and the CAAS directional
# scores behind the nominal/BH activity calls) come from a separate file when one is given
# (the fcs_stats.tsv of the CAAS report). A report ranked by its own score, such as the
# RER one, is then annotated with the CAAS, FADE and accumulation flags of each gene.
# Rankings always come from `stats`, annotation from `annot`; without an overlay `annot`
# is `stats` itself (the CAAS report carries its own flags).
annot <- stats
if (!is.null(params$annot_file) && file.exists(params$annot_file) &&
    !grepl("^NO_", basename(params$annot_file))) {
  annot <- readr::read_tsv(params$annot_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (!"gene" %in% names(annot)) {
    gcol <- intersect(c("Gene", "GENE"), names(annot))[1]
    if (!is.na(gcol)) annot <- dplyr::rename(annot, gene = !!gcol)
  }
}
flag_cols <- grep("^flag_", names(annot), value = TRUE)

# GMT directory: the parameter, else the dat/ directory of the module.
gmt_dir <- if (!is.null(params$gmt_dir) && nzchar(params$gmt_dir)) params$gmt_dir else file.path(this_dir, "..", "dat")
if (!is.null(params$enrich_file) && file.exists(params$enrich_file)) {
  # A presentation-only render reads descriptions, not scientific GMT objects.
  gmts <- as.list(list.files(gmt_dir,pattern="[.]gmt$",full.names=TRUE))
} else invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(gmts <- fcs_load_gmts(gmt_dir))))
desc_map <- suppressMessages(fcs_load_descriptions(gmt_dir))
```

# Overview

```{r overview, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Project", "Trait", "Genes (stats)", "Background genes", "Rankings",
            "Flags", "GMT databases", "num.g (min set)", "max.g (max set)", "Significance rules"),
  Value = c(params$project_name, params$traitname, nrow(stats), length(universe),
            paste(ranking_names, collapse = ", "),
            if (length(flag_cols)) paste(sub("^flag_", "", flag_cols), collapse = ", ") else "(none)",
            length(gmts), params$num_g,
            ifelse(is.null(params$max_g) || params$max_g <= 0 || !is.finite(params$max_g), "(none)", as.character(params$max_g)),
            sprintf("BH of permulation: q.perm < %s; Redlich: analytic levels %s and p.perm < %s", params$fdr_thr, params$analytic_levels, params$pperm_thr))
) %>% kbl_html()
```

```{r run, include=FALSE}
# fcs_run_all() over every GMT database is the expensive step. The pipeline runs it as
# independent tasks, one per subset of GMT files (fcs_compute.R, FCS_COMPUTE_BATCHED in
# fcs.nf), and passes the row-concatenated result in enrich_file. The concatenation is
# exact because the BH correction is scoped per database (see fcs_compute.R). Without
# enrich_file (a manual render) fcs_run_all() runs here in a single pass.
if (!is.null(params$enrich_file) && nzchar(params$enrich_file) && file.exists(params$enrich_file)) {
  if (params$score_source == 'caas' &&
      (!file.exists(saved_metadata) || !identical(saved_params$gene_stat,"max")))
    stop("CAAS FCS requires recorded gene_stat=max metadata; rebuild calibrated max slices/results")
  enrich <- readr::read_tsv(params$enrich_file, show_col_types = FALSE,
                             col_types = fcs_enrich_col_types())
} else {
  if (params$score_source == 'caas') stop('CAAS FCS requires the calibrated enrich_file produced by FCS_CAAS')
  # One ranking vector per score_<ranking> column, with the source's missing-score policy.
  rankings <- list()
  for (sc in score_cols) {
    rk <- sub("^score_", "", sc)
    rankings[[rk]] <- fcs_build_vals(setNames(stats[[sc]], stats$gene), universe,
                                    score_source = params$score_source)
  }
  enrich <- suppressMessages(fcs_run_all(rankings, gmts, num_g = params$num_g,
                                         max_g        = params$max_g,
                                         perms_file   = params$perms_file,
                                         fdr_thr      = params$fdr_thr,
                                         p_perm_thr   = params$pperm_thr,
                                         analytic_levels = as.numeric(strsplit(params$analytic_levels, ",")[[1]]),
                                         gene_stat    = params$gene_stat,
                                         score_source = params$score_source))
}
source(file.path(dirname(src), "fcs_selection.R"))
enrich <- fcs_selection(enrich,params$fdr_thr,params$pperm_thr) %>% dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("sig_top"))
# Gene-set descriptions need the full GMT directory, so they are joined after the merge.
dir.create("fcs_results",showWarnings=FALSE)
if(!is.null(params$enrich_file) && file.exists(params$enrich_file)) file.copy(params$enrich_file,"fcs_results/fcs_enrich_input.tsv",overwrite=TRUE)
jsonlite::write_json(as.list(params[c("gene_stat","score_source","num_g","max_g","fdr_thr","pperm_thr","analytic_levels","cluster_similarity","cluster_threshold")]),"fcs_results/fcs_report_metadata.json",auto_unbox=TRUE,pretty=TRUE)
enrich <- enrich %>%
  dplyr::left_join(desc_map, by = c("database", "pathway")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(description = dplyr::coalesce(description, pathway))

if (anyDuplicated(enrich[c("ranking","database","pathway")])) stop("Description join duplicated FCS identity")

# Per-gene attribute table: the annotation flags plus the derived directional
# nominal/BH evidence flags. They come from `annot`, so a per-module report inherits the CAAS, FADE and
# accumulation annotation.
source(if (file.exists("src/evidence_flags.R")) "src/evidence_flags.R" else "evidence_flags.R")
evidence_flags <- fcs_evidence_flags(annot)
attr_df <- evidence_flags
if (length(flag_cols)) attr_df <- dplyr::left_join(evidence_flags, annot[, c("gene", flag_cols)], by = "gene")
attr_cols_all <- setdiff(names(attr_df), "gene")

# A ranking with negative scores is signed (tested two-sided).
score_long <- stats %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, dplyr::all_of(score_cols)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "ranking", values_to = "drv_score") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ranking = sub("^score_", "", ranking))
ranking_signed <- vapply(split(score_long$drv_score, score_long$ranking),
                         function(v) params$score_source == "rer" || any(v < 0, na.rm = TRUE), logical(1))

# The leading edge keeps only the genes that drive each enrichment. In a magnitude ranking
# these are the members with signal (score > 0); gene.vals of fastwilcoxGMT lists every
# member in the universe, including zero-floored genes, and summarizing over those would
# dilute the composition with non-drivers. In a signed ranking they are the members whose
# score has the sign of the enrichment of the set (positive scores for a set enriched in
# the upper tail, negative for one enriched in the lower tail).
leading <- fcs_annotate_leading_edge(enrich, attr_df) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(score_long, by = c("gene", "ranking")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.signed = unname(ranking_signed[ranking])) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(drv_score) &
                  dplyr::if_else(.signed, drv_score != 0 & sign(drv_score) == sign(stat), drv_score > 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-drv_score, -.signed)

# Similarity grouping over selected C>0 sets, independently of formal significance.
enrich <- fcs_add_clusters(enrich, leading,
                           threshold = params$cluster_threshold, method = params$cluster_similarity,
                           selection_col="selected_C",order_fun=fcs_selection_order) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sig = sig_perm %in% TRUE)
has_perm_any <- any(!is.na(enrich$p.perm))
n_sig <- sum(enrich$sig, na.rm = TRUE)

# Shared selection order within each ranking.
ord_sig <- fcs_selection_order

dir.create("fcs_results", showWarnings = FALSE)
enrich$gene_stat <- params$gene_stat
enrich$score_source <- params$score_source
readr::write_tsv(enrich %>% select(-any_of("gene.vals")), "fcs_results/fcs_all_results.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(leading, "fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge.tsv")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("**FCS selection: %d sets with C>0; %d pass BH of permulation (q.perm < %s).**\n\n",sum(enrich$selected_C),sum(enrich$sig_RER),params$fdr_thr))
cat("C = [I(sig_RER) + (I(R05)+I(R10)+I(R15))/3]/2. C is support for selection, not p/FDR or four independent confirmations. Redlich rules are nested. Direction is sign(stat=AUC-0.5), including Redlich-only terms; sets may contain genes of both signs. CAAS top/bottom is independent of RER sign.\n\n")
cat("BH of permulation uses q.perm; R05/R10/R15 use analytic p.adj < 0.05/0.10/0.15 AND p.perm < the recorded threshold. All p/q retain their original ranking/database families.\n\n")
```

# Enriched gene sets {.tabset .tabset-fade}

All C>0 terms are searchable and paginated, in the shared order. `sig_RER` is displayed as **BH of permulation** in both sources. Group and representative describe similarity, independently of formal significance. Full results, including unselected terms, remain accessible below and in the export.

```{r tables, results='asis'}
selected <- bind_rows(lapply(ranking_names,function(rk) ord_sig(enrich[enrich$selected_C & enrich$ranking==rk,])))
.rule_cols <- c("sig_RER","R05","R10","R15")
for(rk in ranking_names) {
 cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n",rk))
 d <- selected[selected$ranking==rk,]
 if(!nrow(d)) {cat("_No sets with C>0; missing empirical evidence cannot satisfy a rule._\n\n");next}
 disp <- d %>% select(database,pathway,description,C,checks,all_of(.rule_cols),stat,p.adj,p.perm,q.perm,direction,cluster_id,is_representative)
 disp <- disp %>% mutate(across(all_of(.rule_cols),~ifelse(.x,"✓","·")),C=round(C,3))
 names(disp)[names(disp)=="sig_RER"] <- "BH of permulation"
 cat(knitr::knit_print(DT::datatable(disp,rownames=FALSE,filter="top",options=list(pageLength=15,scrollX=TRUE,order=list()))))
}
```

# Overall dotplot {.tabset .tabset-fade}

The same selected terms and order as the table, with four marks per term. Filled circles pass the rule; crosses do not. Color describes the sign of AUC-0.5. No equivalent q.perm cutoff is implied for Redlich rules. All terms are shown; representatives are marked with an asterisk.

```{r dotplot, results='asis', fig.width=11}
.emit_sized_plot <- function(p,height_in) {
 f <- tempfile(fileext=".png")
 ggplot2::ggsave(f,p,width=11,height=height_in,limitsize=FALSE,dpi=110,bg="white")
 cat(sprintf('<img src="data:image/png;base64,%s" style="max-width:100%%;" />\n\n',base64enc::base64encode(f)))
 unlink(f)
}
for(rk in ranking_names) {
 cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n",rk))
 d <- selected[selected$ranking==rk,]
 if(!nrow(d)) {cat("_No sets with C>0._\n\n");next}
 d$.label <- paste0(d$database,":",d$pathway," ",stringr::str_trunc(d$description,48),ifelse(d$is_representative %in% TRUE," *",""))
 d$.label <- factor(d$.label,levels=rev(d$.label))
 plot_d <- tidyr::pivot_longer(d,all_of(.rule_cols),names_to="rule",values_to="passes")
 plot_d$rule <- factor(plot_d$rule,levels=.rule_cols,labels=c("BH of permulation","R05","R10","R15"))
 plot_d$direction <- factor(ifelse(is.na(plot_d$direction),"unavailable",plot_d$direction),levels=c("positive","negative","zero","unavailable"))
 p <- ggplot(plot_d,aes(rule,.label,colour=direction,shape=passes))+geom_point(size=3)+
   scale_shape_manual(name="Rule passed",values=c(`TRUE`=16,`FALSE`=4),drop=FALSE)+
   scale_colour_manual(name="Sign of AUC-0.5",values=c(positive="#b2182b",negative="#2166ac",zero="#555555",unavailable="#aaaaaa"),drop=FALSE)+
   labs(title=paste(params$project_name,rk),x=NULL,y=NULL)+theme_minimal(base_size=10)+theme(legend.position="bottom")
 .emit_sized_plot(p,max(4,2.5+.32*nrow(d)))
}
```

# Leading-edge composition {.tabset .tabset-fade}

The same C>0 selection and order as the table and dotplot. Percentages describe genes with each attribute. Both RER signs are shown within every CAAS ranking. Sets with no retained leading-edge genes remain present with n_le=0 and unavailable percentages. Similarity groups do not filter the table.

```{r leadingedge, results='asis'}
disp_names <- c(flag_rer_acc="RER positive",flag_rer_decc="RER negative",flag_rer_acc_adjusted="RER positive BH",flag_rer_decc_adjusted="RER negative BH")
le_comp_all <- list()
for(rk in ranking_names) {
 cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n",rk))
 d <- selected[selected$ranking==rk,]
 if(!nrow(d)) {cat("_No sets with C>0._\n\n");next}
 le <- leading %>% filter(ranking==rk) %>% semi_join(d,by=c("ranking","database","pathway"))
 want <- attr_cols_all
 summ <- if(nrow(le)) fcs_leading_edge_summary(le,want) %>% select(-any_of(c("ranking","stat","p.adj"))) else tibble(database=character(),pathway=character(),n_le=integer())
 # A left join retains zero/NA-direction and empty-leading-edge selected terms.
 summ <- d %>% select(ranking,database,pathway,description,C,checks,all_of(.rule_cols),direction,q.perm,cluster_id,is_representative) %>%
   left_join(summ,by=c("database","pathway")) %>% mutate(n_le=replace_na(n_le,0L))
 # Preserve consumer aliases while keeping canonical grouping fields.
 summ <- summ %>% mutate(Description=description,Group=cluster_id,Rep=ifelse(is_representative %in% TRUE,"X",""))
 le_comp_all[[rk]] <- summ
 show <- summ %>% select(-Description,-Group,-Rep)
 present <- intersect(names(disp_names),names(show)); names(show)[match(present,names(show))] <- disp_names[present]
 show <- show %>% mutate(across(all_of(.rule_cols),~ifelse(.x,"✓","·")),C=round(C,3))
 names(show)[names(show)=="sig_RER"] <- "BH of permulation"
 cat(knitr::knit_print(DT::datatable(show,rownames=FALSE,filter="top",options=list(pageLength=15,scrollX=TRUE,order=list()))))
}
le_comp_export <- bind_rows(le_comp_all)
readr::write_tsv(le_comp_export,"fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge_composition.tsv")
```

# Methods

CAAS ranks genes by `-log10(p.gen)` calibrated from the raw gene maximum (`gene_stat=max`). The observed
p uses `(1 + count) / (N_valid + 1)` and each null cycle uses leave-one-out
comparisons against the other cycles. Absent raw CAAS scores are filled with zero
before calibration. Without a usable null, calibrated CAAS pathway tests are unavailable.
RER uses the signed parametric score `sign(Rho) * -log10(P)`.

Every gene set of every GMT database is tested against each ranking with the
**Wilcoxon-AUC test** (`RERconverge::fastwilcoxGMTall`), a rank-sum test that asks
whether the genes of the set sit systematically higher in the ranking than the other
genes of the universe. Its statistic, the **AUC** (`stat + 0.5`, range 0 to 1), is the
probability that a random gene of the set outranks a random gene outside it; 0.5 means
no shift. On a ranking where most genes score 0 the analytic p accounts for the ties
(the variance of the rank sum carries the tie term). RER is tested two-sided,
regardless of the observed signs; a set can be enriched on either side. Other rankings
use a two-sided test when they contain negative values, and a one-sided test otherwise.

For RER, genes without an association statistic are excluded from the observed
ranking; measured zero statistics remain. Missing null statistics are excluded
separately within each permulation. CAAS uses the tested background, filling genes
without a score with zero. Each GMT database restricts its background to annotated genes.

The analytic p (`p.adj`, BH within the database) assumes independent genes and species.
The decision rests on the **permulation p** (`p.perm`) instead: the same test is run on
every column of a null built by reassigning the phenotype across species on the real
tree, and `p.perm` is the fraction of null columns at least as extreme as the observed
one, with a pseudo-count. The compared statistic is `AUC - 0.5`: CAAS magnitude
rankings use the upper tail (`stat_null >= stat_observed`), targeting concentration
among genes with stronger convergence evidence. Signed RER rankings use both tails
(`abs(stat_null) >= abs(stat_observed)`). Both use `(1 + count) / (1 + valid cycles)`.
The analytic p is a separate column and is not the permulated quantity. Sets need
at least three annotated background genes outside the set on each side of the calculation.

* **BH of permulation** (`sig_RER`; producer alias `sig_perm`): `q.perm` below `r params$fdr_thr`, where `q.perm` is
  the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment of `p.perm` within each ranking and database.
* A ranking without a permulation null has no `p.perm` and so no significant set.

**Analytic rule (Redlich et al. 2024).** The rule published with RERconverge calls a set
enriched when its analytic BH-adjusted p (`p.adj`) is below a level and its permulation
p is below `r params$pperm_thr`, the permulation p being used as a filter and not corrected
for multiple testing. It is reported next to the rule above as `redlich_level`: the smallest of
the levels `r params$analytic_levels` that the set meets (empty when it meets none). It does not
change `sig_perm`; it contributes to C and selection before similarity grouping. Neither rule imposes a positive-statistic filter.

The selected sets (`C>0`) are ordered by C descending, checks descending, q.perm, p.perm, database and set identity. The order does not depend on direction. Greedy grouping uses leading-edge Jaccard >= the saved threshold (default 0.5) within each ranking. Representatives follow this same order; grouping changes presentation only, with every selected term retained. Empty leading edges form their own groups.

# Method

```{r method, echo=FALSE}
cat("Test       : Wilcoxon-AUC (RERconverge::fastwilcoxGMTall); RER always 'two.sided'; other rankings 'greater' unless they contain negative scores\n")
cat("Null       : AUC - 0.5 per null column; upper tail for magnitude rankings, absolute statistic for signed rankings; pseudo-count (1 + n) / (N + 1)\n")
cat("BH of permulation: q.perm < ", params$fdr_thr, " (BH on p.perm per ranking and database)\n", sep = "")
if (params$score_source == "rer") {
  cat("Universe   : genes with a non-missing RER statistic; measured zeros retained; null NA excluded per permulation\n")
} else {
  cat("Universe   : cleaned_background; no-signal genes floored to 0 (zero-floor)\n")
}
cat("Groups     : greedy by shared C/checks order over C>0, leading-edge ", params$cluster_similarity, " >= ", params$cluster_threshold, " to a representative\n", sep = "")
cat("Analytic   : p.adj < level and p.perm < ", params$pperm_thr, ", levels ", params$analytic_levels, " (Redlich et al. 2024; redlich_level)\n", sep = "")
cat("Order      : C descending, checks descending, q.perm, p.perm, database, pathway\n")
```

## Summary

This report presents Functional Class Scoring (FCS) enrichment results for
**`r params$traitname`** across `r length(gmts)` GMT database(s) and
`r length(ranking_names)` ranking(s) (`r paste(ranking_names, collapse = ", ")`),
tested with the Wilcoxon-AUC test and called significant on the BH-adjusted
permulation p as described in Methods above. `r n_sig` set(s) are significant.
